name: effect
one_liner: A toolkit that helps professional developers write more reliable, bug-resistant TypeScript applications by handling errors and async code in a more structured way.
buyer: A CTO at a growing startup whose TypeScript codebase has become fragile, wanting more maintainable, production-grade code.
business_use_cases: A fintech startup adopts it to reduce runtime crashes from unhandled errors in critical payment-processing code.
A consultancy that builds backend systems for clients standardizes on it to deliver more reliable code, using it as a selling point in pitches.
A training company builds a paid course or certification around it as more companies adopt it and need to upskill engineers.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid consulting and migration services helping companies adopt it in existing codebases, since the learning curve is steep.

steal_this: This weekend, write and sell a focused 'migrate your Express app in a weekend' guide to TypeScript developers.
